entries.title: Micah 7:1
segments:
Woe is me; the prophet laments the absence of good men, and the universal corruption that abounds in the land.  The picture suits well the reign of Ahaz. 
 
  There is no cluster; no gleaning left after the vintage.  I can find no good man with whom to commune.

entries.title: Micah 7:2
segments:
The earth; here used with reference to the prophet's own people. 
 
vv 2-4. 
 
When good men are removed from a nation and the wicked take their place, filling the land with crimes, it is a sign that the day of divine visitation draws near.

entries.title: Micah 7:3
segments: So they wrap it up; rather, "so they pervert it; that is, so they pervert judgment.

entries.title: Micah 7:4
segments: The day of thy watchmen and thy visitation cometh; either, the day of calamity foretold by thy watchmen, that is, the true prophets; or the day of punishment appointed for thy watchmen; meaning the unfaithful watchmen of Judah.

entries.title: Micah 7:5
segments:
vv 5-6. 
 
  Trust ye not--his own house; truth and righteousness have disappeared, so that no one can trust his nearest friends.  Our Saviour applied the words of
to the persecutions which his disciples were to suffer from the ungodly members of their own household.

, etc. 
 
The tendency of sin is to destroy all truth and confidence in the tenderest relatins of life.  This was most fully manifested in the Jews of our Saviour's day, who not only rejected him themselves, but persecuted to the death those of ther own household who embraced his gospel.  Thus they showed themselves to be "vessels of wrath fitted to destruction," and wrath came upon them to the uttermost.

entries.title: Micah 7:7
segments: In the darkest and most degenerate times, we may always wait on God with confident assurance that he will hear and save us.

entries.title: Micah 7:8
segments: Rejoice not against me, O mine enemy; the daughter of Zion is the speaker, and her enemy is the heathen persecutors, represented in like manner as a female.  Compare the expressions, "daughter of Babylon,"
, etc.; "daughter of Chaldeans,"
; and "daughter of Edom,;

. 
 
vv 8-13. 
 
For her unfaithfulness and multiplied transgressions the church of God must patiently bear his chastisements, thought they be severe and long continued; assured that in the end he will bring her forth to the light, and put to shame all her enemies.

entries.title: Micah 7:11
segments: Shall the decree be far removed; "the decree"seems to be here the oppressive enactments of the heathen persecutors.

entries.title: Micah 7:12
segments: He shall come; rather, "one shall come;" that is, collectively, they shall come to thee from Assyria and all the surrounding regions; shall come to submit themselves to thy authority. See

entries.title: Micah 7:13
segments: Shall be desolate; shall first be desolate before the promise can be fulfilled.

entries.title: Micah 7:14
segments:
Feed thy people; the prophet's prayer to Jehovah in the name of his people. 
 
  Thy rod; thy shepherd's rod,

. 
 
  Which dwell--Carmel; Carmel is the image of fertility,
.  In
, dwelling in the wilderness, that is, "solitarily," and sleeping in the woods, are images of unmolested quiet, shelter, and security.  See

. 
 
vv 14-17. 
 
God's faithfulness and truth are pledged to subdue the nations  of the world to his Son Jesus Christ.  They must either willingly receive him, or be broken in pieces by his iron rod.

entries.title: Micah 7:15
segments: According to the days--marvellous things; this is God's answer to his people's prayer.

entries.title: Micah 7:16
segments:
At all their might; at the impotency of all their boasted power against God's people. 
 
  Shall be deaf; stunned and confounded at the hearing of God's wondrous works for his people.

entries.title: Micah 7:17
segments: Shall lick the dust; crouch before God's people.
Their holes; their fastnesses.  See

, where the same Hebrew word is rendered "close places." 
 
  Like worms; creeping away with terror.  It is a characteristic of the prophets, that they close with glorious promises to God's people.

entries.title: Micah 7:18
segments:
vv 18-19. 
 
The time is coming, even in this world, when God shall take away the rebuke of his people from off the earth, and grant them a universal victory over the kingdom of Satan; and "at the resurrection of the just," the whole redeemed church shall obtain a complete and everlasting deliverance from sin in all its effects.
